name: Linguistics
about: Linguistics is the systematic study of human language. It examines how language works: how it is produced and processed in the mind, how it develops in children, how it is used in society, and how it changes over time. The undergraduate major introduces students to phonological, grammatical, and semantic structure as well as descriptive, experimental, computational, and historical approaches to linguistics. Students explore how language interfaces with the social sciences, humanities, and sciences, often taking complementary coursework in related fields. All students complete a senior essay, and many use their linguistics background in careers ranging from technology and education to law and cognitive science.
